prompt: We rolled out a new pricing page to 3 of our 8 markets while 5 kept the old page. In the year before the rollout, the 3 treatment markets were growing 25% faster in conversion than the 5 control markets. After rollout, all 8 markets converged to similar growth rates. Our DiD estimate shows the new pricing page boosted conversion by +8%. Should we trust this?
assertions: Claude explicitly flags that the 25% faster pre-rollout growth in treatment markets violates the parallel trends assumption that DiD requires
Claude explains that the observed convergence after rollout is consistent with trend mean-reversion, not necessarily a causal effect of the pricing page
Claude does NOT accept the +8% DiD estimate as valid without addressing the pre-trend differential
Claude recommends visualizing and testing pre-period trends as a prerequisite, and notes that the current evidence does not support a causal interpretation of the +8% estimate
